{{short description|British statistician}}
{{other uses}}
'''Jennifer Kaye Rogers''' is a British statistician. She was the Director of Statistical Consultancy Services at the [[University of Oxford]] and an associate professor at Oxford{{r|cv|ox}} before joining [[contract research organisation]] PHASTAR in August 2019.<ref name=phamiweb>{{cite news |last1=Wood |first1=Mike |title=Jennifer Rogers named Head of Statistics at CRO Phastar |url=https://www.pharmiweb.jobs/article/oxford-university-statistical-consultancy-director-joins-phastar-as-the-head-of-statistical-research/ |work=PharmiWeb.jobs |date=15 August 2019}}</ref>

Her research has involved [[point process]]es and making inferences from the dropout times of repeated events, as well as applications of statistics to [[clinical trial]]s for [[heart disease]]. She is also active in presenting statistics to the public.{{r|vprss|jrms}}

==Education and career==
Rogers studied statistics at [[Lancaster University]] with the plan of working in the pharmaceutical industry.{{r|jrms}} She earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics with statistics from [[Lancaster University]] in 2006, completing a master's degree in statistics at Lancaster in 2007.{{r|cv}} While at Lancaster, she became more interested in statistical methodology and, following that interest, moved to the [[University of Warwick]] for doctoral study in statistics.{{r|jrms}} She completed her Ph.D. in 2011. Her dissertation, ''Statistical Models for Censored Point Processes with Cure Fractions'', was supervised by [[Jane Hutton]].{{r|cv}}

After working as a research fellow and lecturer at the [[London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine]],{{r|cv|jrms}} and as a post-doctoral research fellow at Oxford, she became Director of Statistical Consultancy Services at Oxford in 2016, and associate professor in 2019.{{r|cv}} She joined [[contract research organisation]] PHASTAR as head of statistical research in August 2019.<ref name=phamiweb/>

==Service==
Rogers is vice president for external affairs of the [[Royal Statistical Society]].{{r|cv|vprss}} She was the 2018 president of the Mathematical Sciences Section of the [[British Science Association]].{{r|cv|presbsa}}

==Recognition==
Rogers was chosen as the Guy Lecturer for 2014 by the Royal Statistical Society.{{r|guy}}
At Oxford, Rogers won an MPLS Impact Award in 2018 for her "contribution ... to the engagement of young people and non-statisticians with the application of statistics".{{r|mpls}}
